title: Launch consent evidence survives deleting its Launch or source

source.ref: Production catalog 2026-10-28: launch_list_attestations.launch_id NOT NULL ON DELETE CASCADE, so deleting a Launch erased the consent evidence for an imported list. Owner chose to keep minimal evidence (wording version, answer, time, pseudonymous original ids). Fix lands as supabase/migrations/20270346027100_launch_consent_retention.sql in #4300.

detail:
Forward repair (20270346026000_vera_launch is applied and is never reapplied). launch_id becomes nullable with ON DELETE SET NULL; launch_ref and source_ref hold the original ids with no foreign key, stamped by a BEFORE INSERT trigger that also refuses a source from another Launch; a BEFORE UPDATE trigger allows only the foreign-key detach; a BEFORE DELETE trigger refuses deletes; service_role keeps SELECT and INSERT only. Owner reads stop once evidence detaches. Evidence deleted before the repair cannot be recovered (the production table held 0 rows on 2026-10-28). A privileged database owner can still bypass these controls. Not decided and not built: retention period, legal holds, subject requests, who may purge, audit of privileged access. pgTAP in supabase/tests/launch_consent_retention.test.sql (19 assertions); HTTP acceptance (owner, stranger, anonymous, service role, source and Launch deletion) in scripts/staging/launch-api.mjs.

Open until migration 20270346027100 is applied to production and merged with #4300; its probe fails until then.

Forward migration 20270346027100 makes launch_id detach on delete, keeps launch_ref and source_ref, and guards writes. Merged with #4300 after the SQL was applied to production.
